item.title: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue
item.description: Iran says the U.S. is seeking changes to a seven-day ceasefire proposal Trump rejected last month as indirect talks continue.

item.title: Electricity bills force 1 in 5 to cut back on food, survey finds
item.description: Americans living on a fixed income are particularly vulnerable when electricity costs surge, a Consumer Reports expert says.

item.title: Russia says Ukraine must make "necessary decisions" to end the war
item.description: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff, meeting with Vladimir Putin in Russia, voiced hope for new trilateral talks involving Ukraine, and Moscow indicated the talks could resume in November.

item.title: Supreme Court rejects bid to restrict treatments for trans inmates
item.description: In an unsigned order, the Supreme Court rejected an emergency appeal seeking to revive a policy ending certain medical treatments for transgender inmates.

item.title: Witkoff blasted for calling Putin a "humanitarian"
item.description: After special envoy Steve Witkoff told Putin he was a "humanitarian" for releasing a U.S. citizen deemed to have been wrongfully detained, GOP Sen. John Cornyn responded, "No. Putin is a stone cold killer."

item.title: Chemical leak in Toledo forces evacuations, shelter-in-place
item.description: A massive chemical leak in Toledo, Ohio, is forcing some people out of their homes while others have been told to shelter in place.

item.title: What we know about death of U.S. green card holder in ICE custody
item.description: Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias, a Mexican-born U.S. green card holder, died while in the custody of Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Texas. He is the 27th person to die in ICE custody this year. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more details.

item.title: Prince Harry says "most important thing is to reconcile" with his family
item.description: Prince Harry says he is eager to reconcile with his family. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Cornell defends its leadership in response to Jane Doe letter
item.description: Officials at Cornell University are disputing claims made by Jane Doe about how the school's leadership responded to her sexual assault allegations. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Khrushchev's great-granddaughter on Stephen Hubbard's release, Witkoff calling Putin a humanitarian
item.description: Russia freed an American citizen it had detained for years after U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin over the future of the Ukraine war. Nina Khrushcheva, the great-granddaughter of former Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev and a professor of international affairs at The New School, weighs in.

item.title: Ohio race takes ugly turn with Ramaswamy ad featuring Acton's mom
item.description: Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother calls her a liar in a new Ramaswamy campaign ad. Acton's brother says the ad marks a "despicable low" and says their stepfather sexually abused Acton when she was a child.

item.title: Knicks championship ring maker on inspiration behind his design
item.description: Jason Arasheben has designed championship rings for plenty of teams. When he was tapped to create one for the Knicks, he knew it needed to represent New York in a special way.

item.title: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger has "a lot of merit." Here's why.
item.description: Combining SpaceX and Tesla, whose stocks jumped after Musk said the companies are exploring a deal, would be the biggest corporate merger of all time.

item.title: George W. Bush's brother says he voted for Talarico in Senate race
item.description: "My vote was motivated by two things: deep concern about Ken Paxton's record and genuine admiration for the character and principles I see in James Talarico," Neil Bush posted on Facebook.

item.title: Witkoff calling Putin a humanitarian is "cringeworthy," former U.S. ambassador says
item.description: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff called President Vladimir Putin "a humanitarian" after the Russian leader released a U.S. citizen who had been imprisoned by Russia since 2022. Former U.S. ambassador William Taylor shares his thoughts.

item.title: Trump weighs moving White House press corps out of building
item.description: Outside allies of President Trump have recently pushed the idea of moving the White House press corps to another building, including former Trump strategist Steve Bannon, one source said.

item.title: Man behind the Knicks' championship ring on capturing New York's grit and energy in design
item.description: Luxury jeweler Jason Arasheben, known as "Jason of Beverly Hills," has made a name for himself designing for the stars and across professional leagues. He gives "CBS Mornings" the first up-close look at his one-of-a-kind design for the New York Knicks championship ring.

item.title: DOJ watchdog declines investigation in Reflecting Pool case
item.description: Hearn's lawyers complain the inspector general has referred the case to the Office of Professional Responsibility, a unit that was largely gutted and lacks independence.

item.title: Polymarket removes bets on outcome of Cornell sexual assault case
item.description: The market had amassed $450,000 in wagers by the time it was pulled from the international platform.

item.title: Cartel-linked mom wanted for child's 1997 murder caught in Mexico
item.description: Anna Marlene Somoza is now awaiting extradition to the United States, where she will face first-degree murder charges, officials said.

item.title: Armed federal agents knock on doors looking for noncitizen voters
item.description: Armed and in uniform, agents from the Department of Homeland Security have been knocking on doors to ask residents about their immigration status whether they're registered to vote.

item.title: Musk chose to restrict Ukraine's access to SpaceX network, sources say
item.description: A decision by Elon Musk led to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's satellite communications network, people familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Iran touts closest ever ties with Russia, contradicting Trump
item.description: Iran says its ties with Russia are stronger than ever after a visit by Putin's top envoy, challenging Trump's assertion that Moscow isn't helping Iran in the war.

item.title: Cornell responds to Jane Doe letter saying she felt disbelieved
item.description: Cornell has denied claims made in a letter from a former student, known as Jane Doe, about a remark by the school's president.

item.title: Cornell faculty member alleges "silencing of Jane Doe's voice"
item.description: Some Cornell faculty members say a letter from Jane Doe in which she said she "felt unsupported and disbelieved" by university president Michael Kotlikoff was not shared with them.

item.title: French government extends curfews after riots sweep across the country
item.description: French authorities are extending curfews and increasing the police presence in public spaces as President Emmanuel Macron's government tries to regain control after rioters torched buildings and looted thousands of businesses this weekend.

item.title: Trump says U.S. will pay fraud whistleblowers, and he'll decide who is paid
item.description: President Trump said successful whistleblowers will get 1% of any fraud they report, although there may be limits.

item.title: Teen girls vape more than boys, study shows
item.description: A new study shows that more teen girls are vaping than boys. This comes after Selena Gomez recently shared that vaping changed her voice. Dr. Abbey Masonbrink, a pediatric hospitalist at Children's Hospital Los Angeles, explains what could be the driving factor in the increase in vaping. Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Watch: Voter who lives near data center confronts Vance on "unbearable" outdoor conditions
item.description: A voter whose family lives right across from a data center confronted Vice President Vance about "constant noise," saying spending time outdoors has become "unbearable."

item.title: Vance says admin. must take action when ICE agents "screw up"
item.description: Vice President JD Vance acknowledged that there are some federal immigration officers "who really screw up."
